Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT B KS-733 PASS (#877, tier 1)** — `73f7e2b2b` (2026-09-06 23:16→23:35 AEST; seven tampers, `index.ts` byte-identical after all seven, both suites re-run green at baseline AND after restore) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It answered the builder's own weakest-point question and then told me NOT to spend the budget on it** — the separate-stores property holds and is stronger than claimed (express-rate-limit 7.5.1 gives each `rateLimit()` call its own MemoryStore by library default at `dist/index.cjs:678`), driven with a PLANT (one shared store → the second prefix 429s at Remaining 0) so the green is information. **F3 MAJOR: the parity cell compares only `windowMs` and `max`** — `skip: () => true` and moving the mount after `createProxyRoutes` both keep the suite **4/4 GREEN** while driving to **no 429 at all**, mechanism confirmed at `proxy.ts:328`. **F4 MAJOR: the gate is purely RELATIVE** — both mounts to `max: 5000` stays green while the published spec advertises 10 on nine operations forever. **F5 is the find of the session and it refused to round it:** four path spellings (`//mfa`, `%6Dfa`, `mfa;x=1`, `mfa%2Fdisable`) dodge EVERY path-scoped gateway limiter, the spec gate falls through by design at `:1047`, and **express's own prefix strip normalises the dodge away AFTER the limiter was skipped** — a class across all seven limiters, `/api/auth/mfa` included. It then named the untested half as decisive and declined to rate it: *"If auth 404s them, F5 is a curio. If auth serves them, F5 is a Blocker on the whole limiter layer."* **It verified the builder's controls ADVERSARIALLY** (removed the reference mount; planted a bogus prefix) to prove the extractor is not a yes-machine, and proved the spec `--check` non-vacuous with two live plants. Every restore an inverse edit verified by sha256 — no checkout, no rm — and it re-derived the builder's claimed hash itself before tampering. |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT A KS-930 F-3 PASS WITH FINDINGS (#876, tier 1)** — `af954c691` (2026-09-06 23:13→23:31 AEST; own `--shared` clone at the LITERAL SHA with `refs/qa/base` pinned, and it CONFIRMED the trap the brief named — the source repo's local `develop` is `ff5218867`, never resolved `origin/develop`) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It proved the PR UNDERSTATES itself.** The builder showed the hole on one synthetic; the tester appended each spelling to each of the **25 real Dockerfiles** — 25/25 rc 0 FALSE CLEAN at base, 25/25 rc 1 blocked at head, with the canonical form as a blocking control. **It also honoured the fixture-shape warning and built BOTH shapes**, showing a single-write fixture reds pre-fix through the FALLBACK — a block for the wrong reason that would have produced a refutation which was an artefact of the fixture. **FINDING 1 MAJOR: the class was not swept** — `npm add`, `npm install-test`/`it`, **bare `yarn`** (its default verb IS install) and `pnpm add` are still false cleans on all 25 at HEAD; and its fix-shape is structurally better than the obvious one: enumerating verbs **fails OPEN**, so INVERT it — a package-manager invocation in a verb not on a read-only allowlist counts as a write — **fails CLOSED**, the direction the guard's own comment asks for. **FINDING 3: `pnpm i` is caught only BY ACCIDENT** (no left word boundary, so `npm[ \t]+i` matches inside `pnpm i`; control `RUN mynpm i` is newly recorded too). **FINDING 2 is a NEGATIVE RESULT and it refutes WEDNESDAY, not the builder:** the brief's claim that exit-code-only cells would have passed agai
